metric_definitions.label: accuracy (all)
metric_definitions.basis: plain choice reading: selected option with highest probability (default rule); correct / answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: macro-F1
metric_definitions.basis: plain choice reading: selected option with highest probability (default rule); mean of per-class F1 over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: AUROC
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; macro one-v-rest AUROC over options and answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: Brier score
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; multiclass Brier score over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: ECE
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; calibration of selected-answer correctness over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: coverage (target reference 95%)
metric_definitions.basis: target reference 0.95; target-specific CV chosen rule; observed accepted / answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: accepted accuracy (target reference 95%)
metric_definitions.basis: target reference 0.95; target-specific CV chosen rule; observed correct accepted / accepted labelled dev cases

notices: development cases only; the held-out test share was not scored or exposed in this comparison
constraints are reference metadata; this comparison does not filter or select candidates

question.instructions: Which part of Ruff (a Python linter and formatter) does this issue concern?

criteria.linter: Lint rules, their fixes, suppression comments (noqa), import sorting, docstring checks, diagnostics or preview rules.
criteria.formatter: The code formatter: how formatted code looks.
criteria.server: The language server (LSP) and editor integration.
criteria.configuration: Settings, the command-line interface, or selecting which rules are enabled.

question.instructions: Which part of Ruff (a Python linter and formatter) does this issue concern? Classify by the behavior or feature being requested or reported. Use the affected component as the main signal: lint-rule behavior and fixes belong to linter, code layout belongs to formatter, and LSP-specific behavior and settings belong to server.

criteria.server: The language server (LSP), editor integration, and editor-specific settings, including how the server discovers, prioritizes, or applies configuration.
criteria.configuration: General Ruff settings, configuration files, command-line options and behavior, and selecting or enabling rules. Includes how users configure Ruff across CLI workflows.

criteria.configuration: Settings, the command-line interface, or selecting which rules are enabled.

question.instructions: Which part of Ruff (a Python linter and formatter) does this issue concern? Classify by the behavior or feature being requested or reported. Use the affected component as the main signal: lint-rule behavior and fixes belong to linter, code layout belongs to formatter, and LSP-specific behavior and settings belong to server.

criteria.linter: Lint rules, new checks, detection coverage, false positives, rule-specific fixes, suppression comments (noqa), import sorting, and docstring checks. Requests to detect redundant, deprecated, or problematic Python code belong here, including requests without a rule code.
criteria.formatter: Code layout and style produced by the formatter, such as spacing, indentation, line wrapping, and quote layout.
criteria.server: The language server (LSP), editor integration, and editor-specific settings, including how the server discovers, prioritizes, or applies configuration.
criteria.configuration: General Ruff settings, configuration files, command-line options and behavior, and selecting or enabling rules. Includes how users configure Ruff across CLI workflows.
